title: miR-3154: Novel Pathogenic and Therapeutic Target in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
authors: Hou, Qingbin; Liu, Yisi; Hou, Jingjin; Song, Haixu; Zhang, Sijia; Zhang, Yan; Liu, Jing; Zhang, Xiaolin; Ji, Yong; Yan, Chenghui; Han, Yaling
one_liner_zh: 该文研究miR-3154在腹主动脉瘤中的致病机制，虽涉及分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是miRNA-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且未聚焦TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening condition with no effective pharmacological treatments currently available, likely due to our incomplete understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying AAA pathogenesis and progression. In many cardiovascular diseases, circulatory microRNAs are potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. Therefore, we investigated novel microRNAs with diagnostic and therapeutic potential in AAA. METHODS: We performed microRNA expression analysis in aorta specimens isolated from mice with saline-induced or Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced AAA, wherein microRNA-3154 (miR-3154) was identified as a potential key molecule in AAA pathogenesis. We used RNA-sequencing analysis, cell migration assays, immunoblotting, protein interactome analysis, coimmunoprecipitation, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation to determine the role of miR-3154 in AAA pathogenesis, clarify the phenotype, and elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Using high-throughput sequencing, miR-3154 was identified in the aortic tissue of ApoE(-/-) mice with AAA as compared with control mice. Increased miR-3154 expression was confirmed in the early-stage Ang II-induced AAA mouse model and the aortic tissues of patients with AAA. Patients with AAA had higher serum miR-3154 level, which positively correlated with computed tomography-estimated size of the aneurysm. Functionally, miR-3154 dose-dependently aggravated vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching and AAA development, both in vivo and in vitro. In vascular smooth muscle cells, TNS1 (tensin-1) was identified as a direct target of miR-3154. Mechanistically, TNS1 interacts with the R1-R13 domain of TLN1 (talin-1), thereby suppressing Sp1 (specificity protein 1) phosphorylation at Thr739 and upregulating MEOX1 (mesenchyme homeobox 1) expression-a key transcription factor regulating vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching. CONCLUSIONS: We uncovered a novel pathogenic role of miR-3154 in AAA, suggesting its potential as both a therapeutic target and prognostic biomarker.
abstract_zh: 背景：腹主动脉瘤（AAA）是一种危及生命的疾病，目前尚无有效的药物治疗手段，这可能归因于我们对AAA发病机制及进展的分子机制理解尚不完整。在许多心血管疾病中，循环微小RNA是潜在的诊断和预后生物标志物。因此，我们研究了在AAA中具有诊断和治疗潜力的新型微小RNA。方法：我们对盐水诱导或Ang II（血管紧张素II）诱导的AAA小鼠分离的主动脉标本进行了微小RNA表达分析，其中微小RNA-3154（miR-3154）被鉴定为AAA发病机制中的潜在关键分子。我们使用RNA测序分析、细胞迁移实验、免疫印迹、蛋白质相互作用组分析、共免疫沉淀、分子对接和分子动力学模拟来确定miR-3154在AAA发病机制中的作用，阐明其表型，并揭示潜在的分子机制。结果：通过高通量测序，在AAA的ApoE(-/-)小鼠主动脉组织中鉴定出miR-3154，与对照小鼠相比表达上调。在早期Ang II诱导的AAA小鼠模型和AAA患者的主动脉组织中，miR-3154表达增加得到确认。AAA患者血清miR-3154水平较高，且与计算机断层扫描估计的动脉瘤大小呈正相关。在功能上，miR-3154以剂量依赖性方式加重血管平滑肌细胞表型转换和AAA发展，无论在体内还是体外。在血管平滑肌细胞中，TNS1（tensin-1）被鉴定为miR-3154的直接靶标。在机制上，TNS1与TLN1（talin-1）的R1-R13结构域相互作用，从而抑制Sp1（特异性蛋白1）在Thr739位点的磷酸化，并上调MEOX1（间充质同源盒1）表达——这是调控血管平滑肌细胞表型转换的关键转录因子。结论：我们揭示了miR-3154在AAA中的新型致病作用，表明其作为治疗靶点和预后生物标志物的潜在价值。
